correctness.rationale: For a deterministic finite total transition function, all-state AF P_j holds exactly iff every directed cycle hits each marked set. A cycle of length ℓ succeeds with probability ∏_j(1-(1-p_j)^ℓ); mapping components are cycles of rooted labelled trees with T=ze^T, so the weighted set-of-cycles EGF is exp(∑w_ℓT^ℓ/ℓ). Inclusion–exclusion gives the stated product and normalization n!/n^n. Joint falling factorial moments E∏(C_{ℓ,n})_{m_ℓ}=(n)_M/(n^M∏ℓ^{m_ℓ}) give independent Poisson(1/ℓ) limits for any fixed lengths; the missing-cycle tail ≤∑_{ℓ>L}ℓ^{-1}∑_j(1-p_j)^ℓ is uniformly small. Thus the infinite product limit is justified. For r=1 positive coefficients give p_1 identically. For r=2 the exact partial fraction F=1+λ((1-T)^-1-(1-cT)^-1), c=(1-p)(1-q), λ=pq/(1-c), reduces P_n=λ(1-Ec^{K_n}) with P(K_n=k)=(k/n)(n)_k/n^k. Survival P(K_n≥k)=(n)_k/n^k increases strictly for k≥2 in n; c∈(0,1) gives strict increase from pq to λ. Checked boundary n=1, and nondegenerate p_j∈(0,1).

value.rationale: Several natural CTL eventuality obligations on uniformly random deterministic transition systems exhibit a nontrivial correlation and a precise size law: each one-label global requirement has probability p_j, yet two together increase strictly from pq to pq/(p+q-pq), and all r have an explicit non-0–1 limiting law. These are exact finite-state model-checking benchmark quantities for a canonical sparse transition class, and a motivated contrast with high-degree independent-edge 0–1 laws. The underlying mapping species is standard, so value is assigned to the complete joint-probability/interpolation classification, not to rebranding the exponential formula or a few finite checks.
